title: The ZN domain acts as a dynamic switch coordinating multiple-step aminoacylation in bacterial leucyl-tRNA synthetase.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the full coordinate file for PDB 9TJT (1.7 MB mmCIF, 22,466 lines, 8,594 atom records, 7 chains) and pulled RCSB metadata for all four depositions (9TJT 2.87 A, 9TJU 1.78 A, 9TJV 2.28 A, 9TJW 2.24 A, all X-ray, released 2026-08-05). Unzipped the 9.6 MB Europe PMC supplement and read all 20 pages of the supplementary PDF: it contains 11 figures and no data tables. Read the paper's only quantitative table (Table 1) in the full text: 6 enzyme variants x 4 kinetic numbers.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That Supplementary Table S2 lists UniProt accessions for 39 LeuRS sequences and Supplementary Table S3 holds norvaline discrimination factors; those tables were not in the retrieved supplementary PDF, which held figures only. Thermal-shift melting temperatures are shown only as curves in Supplementary Figure S7, not as a numeric table.

a1_downloadable.note: All four structures are public in the Protein Data Bank with no login; I downloaded 9TJT.cif (1.7 MB) successfully.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Kinetic labels (Km in micromolar, kcat in per second) are literal columns of Table 1, though only for 6 enzyme variants.

a3_inputs_present.note: Full atomic coordinates are in the files; variant protein sequences are trivially derivable from one E. coli LeuRS sequence plus the named point mutations.

a4_units_stated.note: Table 1 states units explicitly: Km (Leu) in micromolar and kcat in per second, with standard errors from at least three replicates.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The entire labelled dataset is 6 enzyme variants (wild type, Y43A, D162A, W177A, R178A, Y43A/W177A), two of which have 'n.d.' for Km, plus 4 crystal structures. The checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification; this is two to three orders of magnitude short.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; size was never the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper's four stated accessions (9TJT, 9TJU, 9TJV, 9TJW) all resolve in the Protein Data Bank with the conformational states the text describes.

a8_label_provenance.note: Kinetic values come from real bench assays (thin-layer chromatography of activation and aminoacylation time courses), not from any model's output.

honest_claim_h3: No honest machine-learning claim is possible from 6 measured enzyme variants and 4 crystal structures; any model fitted to this would be describing six numbers.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use enzyme sequence and structure to predict how point mutations change leucine-attaching enzyme speed and substrate affinity.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would train on one bacterial enzyme (Escherichia coli leucyl-tRNA synthetase, the protein that loads leucine onto its transfer RNA) with single amino-acid substitutions, each paired with measured reaction rate and affinity. Verified count: 6 variants.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be kcat (turnover number, reactions per second) and Km (substrate concentration giving half-maximal rate, in micromolar). True values come from thin-layer-chromatography assays of amino-acid activation and transfer-RNA charging, three or more replicates each.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Antibiotic developers targeting this enzyme family (benzoxaboroles such as the anti-Wolbachia compound 6 captured in structure 9TJT) would want to know which residues gate the reaction, but with six variants that question is answered by reading the table, not by a model.

ml_idea: The only machine-learning idea this paper supports is contributing its 6 measured variant kinetic values as held-out test points for an existing mutant-kcat predictor such as DLKcat, EITLEM-Kinetics or RealKcat. That is a single row in someone else's benchmark table, not a project. The four structures are useful as visual evidence of a conformational switch but give no label to learn: a conformational-state classifier trained on 4 structures is not a model.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: four mmCIF files total roughly 7 MB and the kinetic table has 6 rows, so every compute number here is negligible. Cross-validation is left null because 6 rows cannot be meaningfully cross-validated.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the labelled rows in Table 1. It takes thirty seconds and gives 6, which kills the project on A5 before anything is downloaded.

verdict_reason: A5 fails by a wide margin: the whole dataset is 4 crystal structures and 6 enzyme variants with measured kinetics, against a requirement of ~1,500 labelled rows. This is an excellent mechanistic structural-biology paper and a terrible machine-learning substrate; its kinetic numbers are best donated to an existing enzyme-kinetics benchmark rather than modelled.
